'''Guillaume-Jules Hoüel''' (7 April 1823 – 14 June 1886) was a French [[mathematician]]. He entered the [[École Normale Supérieure]] in 1843 and received his doctoral degree in 1855 from the [[University of Paris|Sorbonne]]. He was sought by [[Urbain Le Verrier]] at the [[Paris Observatory]], but chose instead to return to Thaon to study there. In 1859 he began to teach at [[Bordeaux]].

In 1863 Hoüel expressed his doubts about the verifiability of the [[parallel postulate]] of [[Euclid]].<ref>J. Houel (1863) "Essai d'une expositin rationelle des principes fondamentaux de la geometrie elementaire", ''Archiv der Mathematik und Physik'' 40: 171–211</ref>

In 1867 Hoüel produced French translations of two key publications of [[non-Euclidean geometry]]: [[Lobachevski]]'s ''Geometrical Studies on the Theory of Parallels''<ref>J. Hoüel (1867) "Etudes geometriques sur la theorie des parallels", ''Mémoirs de la Société des Sciences Physiques et Naturalles de Bordeaux'' 4: 83–128, reprinted by Gauthier-Villars</ref> and [[Bolyai]]'s ''Science of Absolute Space''.<ref>J. Hoüel (1867) "La Science absolute de l'espace", ''Mémoirs de la Société des Sciences Physiques et Naturalles de Bordeaux'' 5: 189–248</ref>

Hoüel published a four volume work titled ''Théorie Élémentaire des Quantités Complexes''. Volume four, published in 1874, began with a discussion of properties of algebraic operations (commutativity, associativity, distribution, and inverses) and used the algebra of [[quaternion]]s and [[versor]]s to describe [[spherical trigonometry]].<ref>J. Hoüel (1874) [https://books.google.com/books?id=tisLAAAAYAAJ Éléments de la Théorie des Quaternions], Gauthier-Villars publisher, link from [[Google Books]]</ref> However, in 1890 [[P. G. Tait]] revealed his dissatisfaction with Hoüel's changes in notation with text that Tait had given for Hoüel's use. Tait wrote:<ref>[[P. G. Tait]] (1890) [https://archive.org/details/117770257 An Elementary Treatise on Quaternions], 3rd edition, p. vi, [[Cambridge University Press]], link from [[Internet Archive]]</ref>
:The earliest offender in this class was the late M. Hoüel who, while availing himself of my permission to reproduce, in his ''Théorie Élémentaire des Quantités Complexes'', large parts of this volume, made his pages absolutely repulsive by introducing fancied improvements in the notation.

In 1876 Hoüel reviewed a [[Russian language]] quaternion textbook written by Romer (1868)<ref>J. Hoüel (1876) "Principles fundamentaux de la Méthode de Quaternions", ''Bulletin ces Sciences Mathématiques et Astronomique'' 11: 113,4</ref>
